Two reflections in folded symplectic coordinates

A pair of sheet exchanges determines more than a pair of reflection lines. When both exchanges preserve the same folded two-form, their shared tangential direction is the characteristic line of that form. We use this fact to construct canonical spectator coordinates, isolate the remaining two-dimensional change, and normalize it by an actual smooth inverse of a cubic integral. The homogeneous version also changes the last position coordinate; its cubic correction is forced by preservation of the two-form.

The primary source is the reprint of Hörmander III, corrected second printing (1994), Theorems 21.4.4 and 21.4.10, printed pages 307–309 and 316–318, PDF pages 322–324 and 331–333 in this exact edition. We supply the commuting-flow details for the spectator construction and a separate construction of the last two homogeneous positions. Folded forms and symplectic target coordinates proves the folded Darboux theorem and its single-involution version. Simultaneous reflections and flat corrections proves full simultaneous smooth and homogeneous coordinates for the two involutions, including the flat correction.

Our convention is ιHaσ=−da\iota_{H_a}\sigma=-daιHa​​σ=−da, {a,b}=Hab\{a,b\}=H_ab{a,b}=Ha​b. Hamiltonian fields are initially defined off the critical hypersurface, where σ\sigmaσ is nondegenerate. Whenever we use a field on that hypersurface, we prove its smooth extension. All maps and flows are local germs, with neighborhoods shrunk for the finitely many required compositions.

The proof map gives exact current proof dependencies for every construction and solution. The earlier flow and bundle companion F0–F2 proves the smooth transverse and commuting-flow charts used here. The differential-form companion F0–F2 and phase-space lesson supply Cartan's formula, flow pullbacks and Hamiltonian commutator identities. The smooth-descent lesson supplies division with all smooth parameters. These existing proofs are reused directly.

If an involution preserves the field distribution, the section, the initial data and the differential equations with their right-hand sides, uniqueness proves invariance. Preservation of the distribution alone would not suffice for a nonzero right-hand side. Antisymmetric data give an antisymmetric solution when the equations transform accordingly. The same argument controls degrees under dilation: apply a dilation to the function, divide by its prescribed degree factor, and check the identical equations and initial data. A distribution may be preserved even when its individual fields have different weights. For the model (5.16), write ρ=ξn>0\rho=\xi_n>0ρ=ξn​>0, t=ξ1/ρt=\xi_1/\rhot=ξ1​/ρ. On the fold, the ambient radical is

σn=n!2ξ1ρ dξ1∧dx1∧⋀j=2n(dξj∧dxj).(7.1) \sigma^n=n!\frac{2\xi_1}{\rho}\, d\xi_1\wedge dx_1\wedge\bigwedge_{j=2}^n(d\xi_j\wedge dx_j). \tag{7.1} σn=n!ρ2ξ1​​dξ1​∧dx1​∧j=2⋀n​(dξj​∧dxj​).(7.1)

Lf=R∂ξ1,Lg=R(∂ξ1−∂x1),Rc=∂ξn.(7.2) L_f=\mathbb R\partial_{\xi_1},\qquad L_g=\mathbb R(\partial_{\xi_1}-\partial_{x_1}), \qquad R_c=\partial_{\xi_n}. \tag{7.2} Lf​=R∂ξ1​​,Lg​=R(∂ξ1​​−∂x1​​),Rc​=∂ξn​​.(7.2)

Both model maps are involutions. Their product in the order f∘gf\circ gf∘g preserves t,ρt,\rhot,ρ and sends

x1⟼x1+2t,xn⟼xn−23t3.(7.3) x_1\longmapsto x_1+2t,\qquad x_n\longmapsto x_n-\tfrac23t^3. \tag{7.3} x1​⟼x1​+2t,xn​⟼xn​−32​t3.(7.3)

The nonzero radial condition has a substantive role. On an ordinary folded plane times a symplectic spectator plane, take q>0q>0q>0,

σ=u du∧dq+dρ∧dz,Dκ(q,z,u,ρ)=(κq,z,u,κρ).(7.4) \sigma=u\,du\wedge dq+d\rho\wedge dz,\qquad D_\kappa(q,z,u,\rho)=(\kappa q,z,u,\kappa\rho). \tag{7.4} σ=udu∧dq+dρ∧dz,Dκ​(q,z,u,ρ)=(κq,z,u,κρ).(7.4)

8. Exercises with complete solutions

Exercise 8.1 (introductory: the intrinsic direction). Under (1.1)–(1.3), prove (1.4) without using Poisson brackets. Show that a common invariant function is constant along the characteristic leaves on Γ\GammaΓ.

Solution. Invariance under dfdfdf, which is identity on TΓT\GammaTΓ and minus identity on LfL_fLf​, makes σ(v,w)=0\sigma(v,w)=0σ(v,w)=0 for v∈Lf,w∈TΓv\in L_f,w\in T\Gammav∈Lf​,w∈TΓ. Alternation gives σ(v,v)=0\sigma(v,v)=0σ(v,v)=0; these vectors span TMTMTM, so Lf⊂EL_f\subset ELf​⊂E. The same holds for ggg. Distinct lines span the two-dimensional EEE, whose intersection with TΓT\GammaTΓ is the one-dimensional KKK. If a∘f=aa\circ f=aa∘f=a, then da(v)=da(df v)=−da(v)da(v)=da(df\,v)=-da(v)da(v)=da(dfv)=−da(v) for v∈Lfv\in L_fv∈Lf​, so da(v)=0da(v)=0da(v)=0, and similarly for LgL_gLg​. Thus da∣K=0da|_K=0da∣K​=0. Integrating that differential equation along any local nonzero field spanning KKK proves constancy on its local leaves.

It is smooth, tangent to s=0s=0s=0, and there equals 2(1+x2)∂x+∂z2(1+x^2)\partial_x+\partial_z2(1+x2)∂x​+∂z​. The spectator translation remains nonzero while a characteristic component is allowed. Exercise 8.3 (intermediate: canonical pairs by full flows). Let smooth fields Hp,HqH_p,H_qHp​,Hq​ satisfy {p,q}=1\{p,q\}=1{p,q}=1 in a folded neighborhood. With σ(Hp,Hq)=1\sigma(H_p,H_q)=1σ(Hp​,Hq​)=1, verify the pullback identity in (2.6), including the sign, and explain why it is valid on the fold.

Solution. On the section p=q=0p=q=0p=q=0, the two fields are transverse and the section tangent is their σ\sigmaσ-orthogonal. Along the map, the derivatives in q,pq,pq,p are Hp,−HqH_p,-H_qHp​,−Hq​, because the fields commute. Their pairing is −1-1−1, equal to (dp∧dq)(∂q,∂p)(dp\wedge dq)(\partial_q,\partial_p)(dp∧dq)(∂q​,∂p​). A transported section tangent pairs to zero with both fields because both flows preserve σ\sigmaσ. The remaining section pairings give the restricted form. Hence the pullback is dp∧dq+σ∣Ndp\wedge dq+\sigma|_Ndp∧dq+σ∣N​. The derivative is invertible by transversality. All fields, flows and forms used are smooth on the full neighborhood; preservation follows from dιHpσ=−d2p=0d\iota_{H_p}\sigma=-d^2p=0dιHp​​σ=−d2p=0, including on the fold by the extended contraction equation. No nondegenerate ambient inverse on the fold was used.

The identity [Hh,Hq1]=H1/h=−h−2Hh[H_h,H_{q_1}]=H_{1/h}=-h^{-2}H_h[Hh​,Hq1​​]=H1/h​=−h−2Hh​ makes

[Y,Z]=h2(−h−2Hh)−h(−1/h)Hh=0. [Y,Z]=h^2(-h^{-2}H_h)-h(-1/h)H_h=0. [Y,Z]=h2(−h−2Hh​)−h(−1/h)Hh​=0.

The fields are smooth by the division arguments in Sections 4–5, so the identities extend to Γ\GammaΓ. Since deg⁡h=1/2,deg⁡q1=0\deg h=1/2,\deg q_1=0degh=1/2,degq1​=0, (5.5) gives [R,Y]=0[R,Y]=0[R,Y]=0 and [R,Z]=−Z/2[R,Z]=-Z/2[R,Z]=−Z/2. The other two fields in (5.13) have weight zero, the nonzero right-hand side is one, and the section and zero data are conic. Uniqueness therefore gives degree zero for qnq_nqn​.

Exercise 8.7 (intermediate: the required last shift). In dimension four, with ρ>0\rho>0ρ>0, consider the model primitive λ=ρt2dx+ρdz\lambda=\rho t^2dx+\rho dzλ=ρt2dx+ρdz. Compute the pullback by g0(x,z,t,ρ)=(x+2t,z,−t,ρ)g_0(x,z,t,\rho)=(x+2t,z,-t,\rho)g0​(x,z,t,ρ)=(x+2t,z,−t,ρ). Find the position correction that makes it preserve λ\lambdaλ and verify that the corrected map is an involution.

Solution. The pullback is

g0∗λ=ρt2d(x+2t)+ρdz=λ+2ρt2dt. g_0^*\lambda=\rho t^2d(x+2t)+\rho dz =\lambda+2\rho t^2dt. g0∗​λ=ρt2d(x+2t)+ρdz=λ+2ρt2dt.

Its exterior derivative differs by 2t2dρ∧dt2t^2d\rho\wedge dt2t2dρ∧dt, so g0g_0g0​ does not preserve the two-form. A shift z↦z+W(t)z\mapsto z+W(t)z↦z+W(t) adds ρW′(t)dt\rho W'(t)dtρW′(t)dt. Thus W′=−2t2W'=-2t^2W′=−2t2, and the fixed-set condition gives W=−2t3/3W=-2t^3/3W=−2t3/3. Both shifts are odd. Applying the corrected map twice cancels them and restores ttt, so it is an involution. It preserves the primitive exactly, not only its derivative.

Exercise 8.8 (advanced: full nonlinear homogeneous normalization). Take V(b)=2b+4b3V(b)=2b+4b^3V(b)=2b+4b3. Find W(b)W(b)W(b), the exact implicit R(t)R(t)R(t), and the first nontrivial terms of R,S,TR,S,TR,S,T. Check the full conjugacy equations by differentiating identities.

Using W′(R)=−R2V′(R)W'(R)=-R^2V'(R)W′(R)=−R2V′(R), the derivative of V(R)=2tSV(R)=2tSV(R)=2tS, and the two identities for TTT, one obtains

F′=−U(2S+2tS′)−2T−2tT′=−2(US+T)=−2t2. F'=-U(2S+2tS')-2T-2tT' =-2(US+T)=-2t^2. F′=−U(2S+2tS′)−2T−2tT′=−2(US+T)=−2t2.

As F(0)=0F(0)=0F(0)=0, F=−2t3/3F=-2t^3/3F=−2t3/3, proving the last full conjugacy equation. The expansions alone would not prove these full identities.

Exercise 8.9 (advanced: a true excluded radial example). Verify every assertion about (7.4)–(7.5), including the independent reflection lines and the obstruction to the homogeneous marked model.

Solution. The top power is 2u du∧dq∧dρ∧dz2u\,du\wedge dq\wedge d\rho\wedge dz2udu∧dq∧dρ∧dz, with simple zero u=0u=0u=0, and the restricted form is dρ∧dzd\rho\wedge dzdρ∧dz, of rank two. Dilation multiplies each term by κ\kappaκ, and its radial field is q∂q+ρ∂ρq\partial_q+\rho\partial_\rhoq∂q​+ρ∂ρ​, nonzero for q>0q>0q>0. Both maps commute with dilation. Set B(u)=−u/(1+u)B(u)=-u/(1+u)B(u)=−u/(1+u) and A(u)=(1+u)3A(u)=(1+u)^3A(u)=(1+u)3. On a small neighborhood of zero, B(B(u))=uB(B(u))=uB(B(u))=u, A(B(u))A(u)=1A(B(u))A(u)=1A(B(u))A(u)=1, and the only fixed normal value is zero. Thus g2=Ig^2=Ig2=I and its fixed set is Γ\GammaΓ. Since BB′A=uBB'A=uBB′A=u, its full folded-plane pullback is

B dB∧d(qA)=BB′A du∧dq=u du∧dq. B\,dB\wedge d(qA)=BB'A\,du\wedge dq =u\,du\wedge dq. BdB∧d(qA)=BB′Adu∧dq=udu∧dq.

The spectator form is unchanged, so both involutions preserve σ\sigmaσ. At u=0u=0u=0, the reflection lines are R∂u\mathbb R\partial_uR∂u​ and R(∂u−32q∂q)\mathbb R(\partial_u-\tfrac32q\partial_q)R(∂u​−23​q∂q​); they are distinct for q>0q>0q>0. Their span contains the radial vector at the marked point (1,0,0,0)(1,0,0,0)(1,0,0,0). The primitive is ιRσ=−qu du+ρ dz\iota_R\sigma=-qu\,du+\rho\,dzιR​σ=−qudu+ρdz; its restricted value at that point is zero. A homogeneous form equivalence intertwines radial fields and preserves this restricted-one-form condition. The marked model has nonzero restricted value dxndx_ndxn​, so such an equivalence is impossible. All other hypotheses, including distinct reflection lines, hold for this excluded example.

Exercise 8.10 (intermediate: exact top power and product order). Derive (7.1)–(7.3), including all constants, and compute the shifts and cancellation coefficients at t=1/2t=1/2t=1/2.

Solution. We have

d(ξ12/ρ)=2ξ1ρdξ1−ξ12ρ2dρ. d(\xi_1^2/\rho)=\frac{2\xi_1}{\rho}d\xi_1 -\frac{\xi_1^2}{\rho^2}d\rho. d(ξ12​/ρ)=ρ2ξ1​​dξ1​−ρ2ξ12​​dρ.

In the top exterior power, the second term is killed by the spectator dρ∧dxnd\rho\wedge dx_ndρ∧dxn​. Choosing the first folded factor and each of the n−1n-1n−1 spectator factors gives n!n!n!, proving (7.1). At the marked point the differential of ggg sends a variation in ξ1\xi_1ξ1​ to 2∂x1−∂ξ12\partial_{x_1}-\partial_{\xi_1}2∂x1​​−∂ξ1​​; its minus-one line is therefore ∂ξ1−∂x1\partial_{\xi_1}-\partial_{x_1}∂ξ1​​−∂x1​​. The cubic shift has zero differential there. The first reflection line and radial vector are as in (7.2). In f∘gf\circ gf∘g, ggg makes the two shifts and flips ttt; fff flips it back without another shift, giving (7.3). At t=1/2t=1/2t=1/2, V=1,W=−1/12V=1,W=-1/12V=1,W=−1/12, and t2V′=1/2,W′=−1/2t^2V'=1/2,W'=-1/2t2V′=1/2,W′=−1/2. In the opposite product order g∘fg\circ fg∘f, both position shifts have the opposite signs.

The simultaneous folded-form proofs are local on the stated ordinary or conic neighborhoods. The complete canonical relation fold theorem, Airy representation and continuity results remain subsequent work.
